description: AddToWalletButton card details and ephemeral key. iOS hands the ephemeral key object to Stripe as JS sent it; Android keeps Kotlin map text and passes that string to the key update listener, which expects the raw JSON key. iOS builds the wallet pass request from cardDetails and reports a customer cancel as Canceled. On Android a click starts push provisioning, a successful provisioning result tokenizes through a TapAndPay double, and a canceled tokenize sends onCompleteAction.

parityGaps.events.onCompleteAction.error.code: G18: iOS reports a customer cancel as Canceled; Android reports a canceled TapAndPay tokenize as Failed.
parityGaps.ephemeralKey.id: G16: iOS passes the key object through; Android stores JSONObject(map).toString() for the wallet flow.

platformOnly.passRequest.name: iOS builds a PKAddPaymentPassRequestConfiguration from cardDetails; Android reads only cardDetails.description.
platformOnly.passRequest.description: See passRequest.name; Android's use of the description is tokenize.displayName.
platformOnly.tokenize.tokenReferenceId: The token prop is documented as Android only.
platformOnly.tokenize.tokenServiceProvider: The token prop is documented as Android only.
platformOnly.tokenize.network: The token prop is documented as Android only.
platformOnly.tokenize.displayName: Android passes cardDetails.description to TapAndPay; iOS asserts it as passRequest.description.

unasserted.token.fpanLastFour: Android builds the TapAndPay tokenize request from token.id, serviceProvider, and network only, and iOS ignores the token prop, so no production code reads this field.
